entries.plain: Creates a variable whose value can change later. It stays inside the block where it was declared.
Creates a variable that cannot be reassigned. Use it for values that stay the same.
The older way to create a variable. Prefer let or const in new code.
Declares a reusable block of code with a name.
Sends a value back from a function and stops running that function.
Runs a block only when a condition is true.
Runs when the matching if condition was false.
Repeats a block, usually once for each item or a counted number of times.
Repeats a block while a condition stays true.
Prints a value to the browser's developer console. It is the usual way to check what your code is doing.
Finds the first element that matches a CSS selector so JavaScript can read or change it.
Tells an element to run a function when something happens, such as a click.
A short way to write a function. The part before => lists the inputs; the part after is the body.
An ordered collection written with square brackets. Items are numbered starting at 0.
A collection of named values written with curly braces. Read a value with a dot or square brackets.
A text format for data that JavaScript can turn into objects and back again.
Asks a server for data and returns a promise for the response.
The plain text inside an element. Setting it replaces what the element shows.
